answer: Jittered arrival prism. Each identity must submit a fixed count of requests per epoch, with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a required distribution; enforcement checks shape via the prism of timing histograms. Agents whose arrivals are too regular or too bursty get throttled. The quartz budget per epoch is capped and non-transferable across identities. Attackers must sustain plausible gaps, paying compute and coordination for every violet shard of synthetic traffic, making mass identities costly to keep live.
